# Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit
Source: https://llms-explorer.com/tree/atlas-infinite-storage-metering-and-max-storage-limit/

# Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] During public preview the maximum logical-data capacity is 128 TB. An optional cap accepts 1 GB through 128 TB; leaving it unset allows 128 TB, and the configured cap can be increased or decreased after creation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-modify-cluster.md
- [statement] The preview API sets the cap through replicationSpecs[].regionConfigs[].autoScaling.storageConfig.shardSizeLimitGB, documented as 1 through 131072 GB. Its autoScaling nesting does not imply a user-selectable storage auto-scaling switch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-atlas-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/api-docs-generated.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The API reference says that including replicationSpecs while omitting storageConfig or shardSizeLimitGB clears the custom limit; omitting replicationSpecs preserves it. The storage tutorial instead says omitting shardSizeLimitGB during an update leaves the limit unchanged. Treat partial-update behavior as unresolved until verified against the targeted API version. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-atlas-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/api-docs-generated.md
- [statement] A reduction in physical allocated disk space alone is not evidence of lower Infinite logical-data charges. This follows from the documented logical-data meter and the Compass issue warning about physical-storage metrics. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/COMPASS-10970

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For the capacity limit, logical data size means uncompressed collections and indexes, rather than the physical storage provisioned by Atlas. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md
- [statement] Storage grows with data without selecting a per-node disk size or enabling storage auto-scaling. Changing compute tier does not change logical capacity; inference: the configured cap is a capacity guard rather than a reservation for that many provisioned gigabytes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-modify-cluster.md
- [statement] Read effectiveReplicationSpecs[].regionConfigs[].autoScaling.storageConfig.shardSizeLimitGB for the enforced limit; replicationSpecs holds the configured value and may omit it. The generated API reference warns that system-managed changes can make the enforced value differ from the configured value. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-atlas-kubernetes/blob/main/docs/api-docs-generated.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas Infinite meters compute, storage, and backup separately. Storage is billed hourly on uncompressed logical data in gigabyte-hours, independently of compute nodes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-modify-cluster.md
- [statement] Billable cluster storage includes stored database data and local.oplog.rs; backup retention is a separate billing dimension. Deleting application data therefore does not establish that all billable storage or retained history has disappeared. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md
- [statement] COMPASS-10970 states that dbStats/$collStats storageSize and freeStorageSize do not represent meaningful on-disk usage on Infinite. The issue requested hiding those displays and records fix version 1.49.15; it does not prove which client version a customer currently runs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-24) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/COMPASS-10970
- [statement] The Weighted Average analysis warns that Infinite logical capacity and Atlas Core configured disk capacity are different units; its capacity ratios and pricing discussion are analysis of MongoDB documents, not independent metering experiments. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30) — https://theweightedaverage.com/posts/2026-09-30-atlas-infinite-agent-migration-gates/
- [statement] MongoDB engineering describes independently scaled storage architecture, but this alone does not establish unrestricted customer storage capacity; the product storage documentation still specifies the 128 TB preview ceiling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-storage.md · keywords: Atlas Infinite storage metering and max storage limit · also: https://medium.com/mongodb/the-ground-beneath-the-database-408be2d3e055
